title: Place the Cows Far Apart

concept.title: Binary search on the distance, greedy for the check
body: You must place `c` cows in `n` stalls so that the smallest distance between two cows is as large as possible. Ask the yes/no question: "can we place all cows with every two at least `D` apart?" With the stall positions sorted, a **greedy** check answers it: put the first cow in the first stall and always put the next cow in the nearest stall that is at least `D` away from the previous one.

If `D` works, any smaller distance works too, so the answers are "yes ... yes no ... no" and the largest `D` with "yes" can be found by binary search. Because we look for the **largest** good value, use `mid = (lo + hi + 1) // 2` to avoid an endless loop.

statement: A farm has `n` stalls at different positions on a line. Place `c` cows in different stalls so that the smallest distance between any two cows is as large as possible. Print that largest possible smallest distance.
inputFormat: The second line has the `n` stall positions (all different, in any order).
outputFormat: Print the largest possible minimum distance.

examples.note: Place the cows at 1, 4 and 9: the smallest distance is 3.

hints: To test a distance D, place the first cow at the first stall and then each cow in the first stall at least D after the last cow.
Binary search the largest D that fits all cows; use `mid = (lo + hi + 1) // 2`.

explanation: Greedy placement decides whether a distance is possible, and feasibility is monotone in the distance. Binary search finds the largest feasible distance.
solution.complexity: Time O(n log n + n log(range)), space O(1).

code.python:
import sys
input = sys.stdin.readline

n, c = map(int, input().split())
x = list(map(int, input().split()))

x.sort()
lo, hi = 1, x[-1] - x[0]
while lo < hi:
    mid = (lo + hi + 1) // 2
    count = 1
    last = x[0]
    for p in x[1:]:
        if p - last >= mid:
            count += 1
            last = p
    if count >= c:
        lo = mid
    else:
        hi = mid - 1
print(lo)
